pages.title: Tackling Gas and Energy Prices - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Tackling Gas and Energy Prices
Putting gas in your car, cooling your home in the summer, and heating it in the winter are a few of our most basic everyday needs. Yet, we have seen energy prices skyrocket while reliability goes down.
These are unacceptable outcomes. The hard-working, middle-class people of Central and Southern Illinois can’t afford massive price hikes in things so necessary for everyday life.
In Congress, I will fight to bring down the cost of gas by taking action to:
- Take action to freeze the gas tax for immediate relief
- Implement year-round E-15 blend to provide immediate relief at the pump and support Illinois farmers
- As we are dealing with rising costs, boosting domestic oil and gas production and drilling on federal lands to provide short-term economic relief
- Support energy policies that bridge us to a clean energy economy, including supporting natural gas and nuclear energy
- Continue to release oil from U.S. strategic reserves
- Enact a windfall profit tax on oil and gas companies to make sure oil companies aren’t profiting at our expense
- Expand electric vehicles and building a national charging network that is supported with union labor

pages.title: Middle-Class Tax Relief and Fighting Inflation - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Middle-Class Tax Relief and Fighting Inflation
Fighting inflation is the most important issue we are facing. Working people in Central and Southern Illinois are hurting, and they need relief right now. We need a leader in Congress who will fight every day to make sure working families are not getting left behind.
There are some short-term solutions to inflation that Congress needs to act on today to provide immediate relief to working people. But ultimately, this is not a problem that occurred over night. Decades of Democrats and Republicans have contributed by allowing our jobs to be shipped overseas, exporting manufacturing from America to China, and allowing China to become the global economic leader that America used to be. In addition to short term measures, I support ideas that will increase American manufacturing so we can start to make things at home again.
- Repeal the Trump tax cuts that benefit the super-rich over working people
- Extend the child tax cut for working families
- Allow Medicare to negotiate drug prices to lower prescription drug costs
- Cap the cost of life-saving drugs like insulin at $35
- Invest in union apprenticeship programs to promote alternatives to a 4-year college degree and a path to a debt-free, high-paying trades career
- Support the Competes Act to bring manufacturing back to America and decrease inflation by relieving stress on global supply lines

pages.title: Working Families - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Working Families
Fighting for working families is my life’s work. It is what I’ve dedicated my entire career to. For too long, working families in Central and Southern Illinois haven’t had a true advocate in Congress. I want to be that advocate and fight for them. That is the reason I am running for Congress.
Working families, especially in Central and Southern Illinois, are struggling. I believe our recovery from the pandemic should leave no one behind. We should be prioritizing working families and communities of color that have been left behind and disproportionately impacted by COVID19. A fact the COVID-19 pandemic has laid bare and made all the more urgent to address. This would be a top priority in Congress for me.
When I worked for the United Food and Commercial Workers Union, I toured meatpacking facilities and saw union workers—many of them immigrants—working dangerous jobs to provide us with the food we need. In addition to improving safety and working conditions, our union advocated at the state and federal level for access to paid sick leave for workers.
I was proud to work on behalf of fire fighters and first responders to ensure they have the equipment and protections they needed to have safe working conditions.
I strongly believe that when workers can collectively bargain, they not only earn better wages and benefits, but can ensure safer working conditions. I will also be an advocate to make sure workers have a steady and reliable income in retirement after a lifetime of work by protecting hard-earned pensions.
Working with Gov. J. B. Pritzker, legislative leaders, labor and business, I helped lead the fight to pass a $15 minimum wage, making sure nobody who works full time in Illinois remains in poverty. We need to do the same at the federal level.
This is a unique moment in our nation’s history. Long before the pandemic, the gaps between rich and poor in America were an enormous divide. As we work to get our economy back on track and address economic and social injustice that have been part of our economy since long before March 2020, I believe we need a bold agenda to directly benefit working people, especially those who have been hit the hardest by stagnating wages and skyrocketing costs, especially in child care and health care. So many essential workers across Illinois and across the country – from nurses and other health care workers to grocery store workers and fire fighters – have sacrificed so much, and we owe it to them to provide the support they need.
Putting Money in Workers’ Pockets
- Invest in working families, child care, public education, affordable housing, health care, and more while cutting taxes on the middle class, paid for by making those earning more than $400,000 kick in their fair share
- Raise the minimum wage to $15 per hour at the federal level
- Extend the child tax cut and make child care less expensive
- Make health care more affordable by strengthening the ACA and creating a public option
- Create job training programs that give hard-working kids and adults the tools to get a better job or a raise
- Lowering the cost of prescription drugs
Strengthening Workers’ Rights
- Leading the charge to pass the PRO Act
- Pass mandatory paid sick and medical leave
- Guarantee the fundamental right to collectively bargain for better pay, safety conditions, and other job factors
The fact is, too many politicians today have lost sight of the people they were elected to represent in Washington. We need elected leaders who are in it for the right reasons, and are drawn to public service because they truly care about workers. In Congress, I will continue my life’s work of fighting tirelessly for working families, so that all Illinoisans can live dignified lives and earn a living wage.

pages.title: Health Care - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Health Care
I believe that health care is a right, not a privilege.
I was never more aware of the importance of health care than after my nephew was born with Down syndrome and had to have open heart surgery when he was just four months old. Thankfully, my sister’s family had insurance through her employer, and they were able to enroll him in an intervention program when he was just a few months old. Without the coverage they had, they never would have been able to afford the intensive care my nephew received—and that was just in the first few months of his life.
When I was first starting my business, the ability to easily access health care through the ACA was essential in providing the flexibility and stability I needed to get off the ground, but not everyone is so lucky. We need to make health care both more affordable and more accessible for everyone. That is why I support a public option, so we can move our society forward and ensure that everyone—regardless of where they live or work, or how much they earn—can access the care they need.
In Congress, I will work to expand access to telehealth. Americans have greatly benefited from the expansion of telehealth, especially in rural communities like Central and Southern Illinois. Telehealth is more cost effective and provides more flexibility for patients to access care. I will advocate expanding telehealth services on a permanent basis to ensure that telehealth remains an option for Medicare beneficiaries now and after the pandemic.
Unfortunately, too many Illinois families still don’t have access to the affordable, high-quality health insurance that my sister’s family depended on for the health of their family. Despite significant gains under the Affordable Care Act, over 800,000 Illinoisians remain uninsured today. That is unacceptable.
And while many still struggle to access care at all, others find the care they do have is unaffordable. This includes so many seniors who rely on Medicare for their coverage but face ever-rising prescription drug costs from the pharmaceutical industry. That, too, has to stop.
I also support strengthening Medicare and making it work for the nearly 2 million Illinois seniors who depend on it for care. We should find ways to expand Medicare coverage to include dental, hearing, and vision; while also pursuing strategies to make overall care more affordable, such as by allowing Medicare to negotiate for prescription drug prices, lowering the costs for the federal government and seniors alike. Additionally, I believe we need to work toward preventative measures more widely to stave off another pandemic.
Making Health Care More Affordable
- Allow Medicare to negotiate for prescription drug prices so seniors can afford the medications they need
- Expand Medicare coverage to include more services, including dental, hearing, and vision.
- Introduce a public option to keep insurers honest on price hikes
In Congress, I will put people first—not Big Pharma and insurance companies—by working to get more people more affordable health care.

pages.title: Choice - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Choice
I am 100% pro-choice. I believe that a woman should be able to make her own reproductive health care decisions. Those decisions should be made between a woman and her doctor, without the interference of the federal government or anyone else. I know women personally who have faced those decisions, and I understand that they are some of the most difficult that any of us face in life.
I have been horrified by the attacks on women’s reproductive rights that we have seen across the country in recent years, in Texas and other states. Not since before Roe v. Wade has a woman’s right to choose been under such existential attacks, as opponents of choice look to pass more and more restrictive laws that strip us of our rights.
Protecting a Woman’s Right to Choose
- Fight to protect Roe v. Wade from anti-choice attacks, so that women can access safe and legal reproductive health care, regardless of where they live
- Protect Planned Parenthood and other reproductive health care organizations from efforts to defund services for women and families
- Support the repeal of the Hyde Amendment, which limits reproductive health care services for low-income women
In Congress, I will be a steadfast advocate for a woman’s right to choose, so that all women, in Illinois and around the country, are able to access the health care services they need.

pages.title: Immigration - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Immigration
Our immigration system is badly broken and in need of reform. The fact that millions of immigrants continue to live in the shadows in this country—while working essential jobs, paying taxes, and raising families—speaks for itself. We are a nation of immigrants, but too many politicians continue to vilify and scapegoat the very immigrants who we depend on in countless ways, and who are our neighbors, our coworkers, and our friends.
When I worked for the United Food and Commercial Workers Union, I saw firsthand how broken our system really is. I saw a largely immigrant workforce working incredibly dangerous jobs, producing the food that many of us eat without thinking once about where it came from or who played a role in delivering it safely to our grocery stores and dinner tables. Yet instead of prioritizing ways to keep workers safe or crack down on employer abuses of vulnerable workers, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) leadership would order workplace raids to instill fear in immigrant workers and undermine the power of unions like UFCW, which often is the only source of legal help to undocumented immigrants. The Biden administration’s recent guidance halting such workplace raids is a definitive step in the right direction. But we need to do more to protect our essential workers and help undocumented immigrants work legally.
Passing Real Immigration Reform
- Create a pathway to citizenship for DREAMers, farmworkers, and immigrants covered by Temporary Protected Status (TPS)
- Work toward creating pathway to citizenship for the millions of undocumented immigrants already live here and pay taxes
- Protect workers from workplace raids that unfairly target undocumented immigrants while ignoring the problem of employer abuses
- Expand H-2A and H-2B visas to allow employers to fill open positions and get our economy back on track
In Congress, I will work with lawmakers from both parties to pass bipartisan immigration reform that is so long overdue.

pages.title: Environment and Climate Change - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Environment and Climate Change
From the water we drink to the air we breathe and the parks we recreate in, preserving and protecting our environment is among our most essential tasks to ensuring a high-quality, healthy life—for ourselves, our children, and future generations. At the same time, climate change remains an existential threat to all of us, and to our ability to maintain our way of life. But it is also a challenge that comes with the opportunity to reimagine what our economy, our energy systems, and our environment can and should look like.
Here in Illinois, I was part of building a coalition of workers to transition our economy to clean energy. We worked to find solutions to questions about how best to invest in clean energy and what strategies to use to achieve zero carbon emissions. The answers to those questions will shape not just our environment, but our economy for generations to come. As we transition to clean, renewable energy like wind and solar instead of fossil fuels, we need to do so in a way that also creates good-paying, union jobs and doesn’t leave people behind—particularly those who live in communities where environmental injustice has exposed people of color to air pollution and PFAs. Let’s make America a leader in clean energy, creating jobs and reducing our dependence on foreign energy from unstable regimes around the world.
Preserving the Environment
- Provide more funding and resources for clean air and clean water in our communities and strengthen federal air and water protections
- Protect public lands from oil drilling and environmental degradation and parks and open spaces from overdevelopment and contamination
Building a Clean Energy Economy
- Invest in solar, onshore and offshore wind, and other forms of renewable energy to quickly transition the country off of fossil fuels
- Train workers to meet future demand for solar and wind and provide new work and career opportunities in high-paying, high-growth jobs, especially in Central and Southern Illinois communities struggling with job loss and low wages
- Create equity and access to economic opportunity for communities of color across Central and Southern Illinois by making sure that communities of color are recruited for high paying union jobs.
In Congress, I will not pass the buck when it comes to tackling the climate crisis and fighting for clean air and clean water for all of our communities, because the stakes are simply too high not to take action.

Nikki has brought over $288 million in federal grants back to Illinois’s 13th Congressional District. Nikki’s first piece of legislation was the LEAP Act to incentivize small businesses to hire directly from apprenticeship programs.

pages.title: Standing with Workers - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Standing with Workers
I’ve spent my entire career fighting for workers and their families. And as a dues-paying member of the United Food and Commercial Workers Union, I’m continuing this fight in Congress, where I’m focused on passing the PRO Act to protect workers’ rights and improving pathways to good-paying jobs in Central and Southern Illinois.
- After Akorn Pharmaceuticals left working families high and dry with a surprise closure of their Decatur facility, I introduced the Fair Warning Act to strengthen advance notice requirements and ensure that companies are treating working people with the dignity and respect they deserve. I also worked with state and local leaders to successfully attract a new employer to restore jobs at the facility.
- When U.S. Steel tried to use a legal loophole to avoid providing advance layoff notice to 400 Granite City Works employees, I worked with the Governor to secure an investigation by the Illinois Department of Labor. After calling the company out for their actions, they agreed to provide the impacted workers with additional support.
- During my first 100 days in Congress, I introduced bipartisan legislation to help address the job skills gap by supporting the apprenticeship and pre-apprenticeship programs that get folks ready for careers in growing industries. My Leveraging and Energizing America’s Apprenticeship Programs (LEAP) Act will provide tax credits to small businesses to address both the need for more qualified workers and the need to cut educational costs for job seekers – a win-win for employers and employees.
- After hearing about the high upfront cost of purchasing tools for folks interested in pursuing a career in the building trades, I introduced the bipartisan Tools Tax Deduction Act to make it easier for apprenticeship employees and construction workers to afford the equipment their jobs require.
- When our service members return home, it’s critical that we help them find good-paying careers. I’ve introduced bipartisan legislation to expand veterans’ access to jobs in science, technology and health care by making it easier to access STEM scholarships. I’m hopeful that this bill will help us to fill high-demand jobs while ensuring that our heroes have pathways to new careers.
- We’re continuing to face a child care crisis across this country, and our child care workers need urgent help. The child care workforce has been among the slowest sectors to recover from the pandemic, and their wages remain unacceptably low. I’ve been proud to champion investments in our child care system — joining a letterurgingHouse Leadership to extend critical Child Care Stabilization Grants and cosponsoring the Child Care Stabilization Act to provide additional funding to support child care programs and workers.

pages.title: Lowering Costs - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Lowering Costs
Working families in Illinois and across the country are being squeezed by high prices at the grocery store and the gas pump. In Congress, I’m working to bring costs down and give our families and small businesses some breathing room.
- As too many of our families continue to struggle with the extreme cost of child care, we need a middle class tax cut. I’m a proud cosponsor of the American Family Act which would restore the monthly Child Tax Credit and make it permanent.
- Representing some of the top counties in the nation for corn and soybean production, I’m a strong supporter of biofuels. In Congress, I’m working to increase our use of ethanol and Sustainable Aviation Fuel — proven ways to bring down prices at the gas pump and the airport ticket counter.
- There’s no excuse for pharmaceutical companies to charge consumers hundreds of dollars for insulin. That’s why I’ve cosponsored the Affordable Insulin Now Act to cap the price of insulin at $35 a month for all patients.
- I’ve introduced the Rural Energy Savings Act to provide interest-free loans to utilities in order to help families and businesses afford energy efficiency improvements, reducing emissions and saving money at the same time.

pages.title: Creating Jobs - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Creating Jobs
Macon County is the beating heart of manufacturing in Illinois, but we need to do more to spur economic development and the creation of good-paying jobs in our region. As we work to create more good paying jobs, I’m focused on bringing manufacturing back home and investing in a 21st century Heartland economy.
- As Chief of Staff at the Office of Management and Budget in President Biden’s administration, I worked to open the Made in America Office to ensure that American companies and manufacturers get top priority in federal projects.
- In Congress, I launched a Climate Jobs task force to focus on building our clean energy economy with good-paying union jobs in places like Central and Southern Illinois. As a part of that work, I was thrilled to support MachH2’s successful application to establish a $1 billion Midwest Regional Hydrogen Hub to drive American energy production and support new jobs in Illinois.
- Since World War I, a shoe manufacturing company in Belleville has been equipping our military men and women with combat boots. During my first year in Congress I was thrilled to announce a new $7.8 million contract for Belleville Boots and work on a bipartisan basis to support American military equipment manufacturing in the National Defense Authorization Act .
- Our region is also a national leader in the development of cutting-edge agricultural technology. I was proud to advocate for the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign’s Fermentation and Agriculture Biomanufacturing Hub to receive designation as a national tech hub. This designation further establishes the Decatur to Champaign region as America’s Ag Tech Corridor and will help to attract additional federal investment to our region.

pages.title: Supporting Family Farmers - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Supporting Family Farmers
Agriculture is the number one economic driver in Illinois — and communities in Central and Southern Illinois are some of the top producers of corn, soybeans and horseradish in the world. As a member of the House Committee on Agriculture, I’m laser focused on delivering results for our family farmers and rural communities. I’ve formed a bipartisan Agriculture Advisory Council with stakeholders across the 13th District to help me advocate for a strong, bipartisan farm bill that brings agriculture into the 21st century, supports our family farmers and feeds hungry folks across Illinois. I’ll keep pushing my colleagues to get it done.
Rebuilding Rural Communities
From aging infrastructure and a rapidly changing economy to limited access to health care and high-speed internet, our nation’s rural communities are facing an onslaught of generational challenges. In Congress, I’m fighting for investment and support to help our smallest cities and towns survive and thrive in our modern economy. I introduced the Rebuild Rural America Act to invest in economic development and allow the federal government to provide more comprehensive support to rural communities.
Driving Agriculture Research & Development
Central and Southern Illinois are home to some of our nation’s leading agricultural research institutions, but our nation’s investment in this research has fallen behind China and the European Union. I’m working to ensure that the United States can continue to lead the world in food production and food security. That’s why I introduced the America Grows Act to put our money where our mouth is and up our investments in the incredible work being done at places like the University of Illinois, Southern Illinois University Edwardsville and the community colleges and agribusinesses throughout our region.
Supporting the Next Generation of Family Farmers
The average age of an American family farmer is approaching 60 years old, and the success of our rural communities will depend on our next generation entering agriculture. I’ve introduced two bipartisan bills to help bring more young people into the agriculture workforce by making farm and ranch workers eligible for public service student loan forgiveness and help young and beginning farmers gain access to land, markets and capital — the biggest barriers for new and underserved farmers.
Combating Food Deserts
When residents of Cahokia Heights lost access to their local grocery store, I knew we had to do more to ensure that every family has access to healthy, affordable food options — no matter where they live. I’m proud to be a cosponsor of the Food Deserts Act to support grocery stores in areas with limited food access. I’ve also signed on to support the Delivering for Rural Seniors Act and the Enhance Access to SNAP for College Students Act to address food insecurity for Americans of all ages.

pages.title: Advocating for Veterans - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Advocating for Veterans
As the granddaughter of two World War II veterans and a member of the House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs, I’m committed to ensuring that our nation’s heroes receive the benefits they’ve earned and deserve. With the input of my Veterans Advisory Council, I’m working to improve access to services for veterans in our rural communities and to ensure that we’re doing right by our women veterans — the largest growing demographic in the VA system.
- When our service members return home, it’s critical that we help them find good-paying careers. I’ve introduced bipartisan legislation to expand veterans’ access to jobs in science, technology and health care by making it easier to access STEM scholarships. I’m glad that this bill has passed unanimously out of the House Veterans Affairs Committee and I’m hopeful that it will soon help us to fill high-demand jobs while ensuring that our heroes have pathways to new careers.
- There should be no such thing as a homeless veteran. I’ve cosponsored the Return Home to Housing Act to reform the VA’s support for unhoused veterans and improve access to transitional housing and the Health Foundations for Homeless Veterans Act which would help fund transportation, communications services and food supplies for our vets.
- We can never allow our nation’s heroes to be cheated out of their hard earned benefits. I’m proud to be a cosponsor of the GUARD VA Benefits Act to crack down on those seeking to take advantage of veterans by charging unauthorized fees for helping with benefits claims.
- It’s critical that we expand home and community-based services for disabled and elderly veterans. I was proud to support the Elizabeth Dole Home Care Act, which passed the House in our effort to improve access to care and increase the VA’s support for caregivers.
- Women veterans are the fastest growing demographic in our veteran community, but they continue to lack quality access to critical health care services. That’s why I convened a women veterans roundtable with women from Central and Southern Illinois to hear directly about the challenges women vets continue to face. I was glad to take their input back to Washington where I held a Congressional women veterans roundtable to discuss how we can better serve our women vets.

pages.title: Protecting Medicare & Social Security - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Protecting Medicare & Social Security
Social Security and Medicare are a promise that we’ve made to America’s seniors. I oppose any changes that will undercut these vital programs.
- I’ve cosponsored the Social Security Fairness Act , to ensure that public sector workers and their families receive their full Social Security benefits.
- I’ve also cosponsored the Seniors Access to Critical Medications Act to ensure that patients on Medicare can continue to receive critical medications by mail, and allow caregivers and family members to obtain medications on their behalf.

pages.title: Prioritizing National Security - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Prioritizing National Security
The United States has a broken immigration system that weakens our national security and leaves families in legal limbo. We need bipartisan reform to create more pathways to citizenship, protect Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) and ensure that our border is secure. I believe that we need a comprehensive approach to immigration that addresses the causes of the immigration crisis at its root. That’s why I’ve supported funding for stronger border measures, including investments in better border patrol technology between ports of entry, fentanyl detection devices and child welfare professionals at the border.
- I’ve cosponsored the American Dream and Promise Act , which would provide greater protection and stability for certain immigrants, including Dreamers, whose status has remained uncertain for years.
- I’ve advocated for increased federal funding to address the flow of deadly, illicit fentanyl that is exacerbating the opioid crisis in nearly every American community — including in Central and Southern Illinois.

I was proud to stand alongside the United Steelworkers and the Granite City community to hold U.S. Steel accountable. Together, we secured the restart of the blast furnace and the return of 400 good-paying union jobs.
- After Akorn Pharmaceuticals left working families high and dry with a surprise closure of their Decatur facility, I introduced the Fair Warning Act to strengthen advance notice requirements and ensure that companies are treating working people with the dignity and respect they deserve. I also worked with state and local leaders to successfully attract a new employer to restore jobs at the facility.
- When I’m back home, families tell me every day about the challenges of finding and affording quality child care. The child care workforce remains one of the slowest sectors to recover from the pandemic, and far too many child care workers are still paid wages that don’t reflect the essential work they do. That’s why I’ve been proud to champion investments in our child care system, including cosponsoring the Child Care Stabilization Act to strengthen child care programs, support workers, and help ensure families can access the care they need.

pages.title: Lowering Costs - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Lowering Costs
Working families in Illinois and across the country are being squeezed by high prices at the grocery store and the gas pump. It’s frustrating — but it doesn’t have to be this way.
While the Trump Administration wreaks havoc on the pocketbooks of folks in Illinois 13, I’m working to bring costs down and give our families and small businesses some breathing room.
- As too many of our families continue to struggle with the extreme cost of child care, we need a middle class tax cut. I’m a proud cosponsor of the American Family Act which would create a permanent tax cut for working parents.
- Representing some of the top counties in the nation for corn and soybean production, I led the effort to pass legislation in the House allowing the year-round sale of E15 — lowering fuel costs for families, strengthening America’s energy independence, and creating new opportunities for our corn growers.
- There’s no excuse for pharmaceutical companies to charge consumers hundreds of dollars for insulin. That’s why I’ve cosponsored the Affordable Insulin Now Act to cap the price of insulin at $35 a month for all patients.
- I’ve heard from countless independent pharmacists across the district about how they’re being squeezed out of business by Big Pharma and the health insurance corporations – coordinated by greedy middlemen called Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs) who work to keep drug prices artificially high. That’s why I’m a proud cosponsor of the Pharmacists Fight Back Act , which would crack down on predatory drug pricing practices and expand patient choice.
- The Affordable Care Act’s enhanced tax credits saved families hundreds of dollars a month on their health insurance premiums. When the Trump Administration let those credits expire, costs surged for working families. I’m working to restore and extend these savings so families can keep more of their hard-earned money while maintaining access to affordable health care.
- I’ve introduced the Rural Energy Savings Act to provide interest-free loans to utilities in order to help families and businesses afford energy efficiency improvements, reducing emissions and saving money at the same time.

pages.title: Creating Jobs - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Creating Jobs
Central and Southern Illinois is the beating heart of manufacturing growth in the state, and its workers represent the best of what makes America strong. But the challenges facing our region are the same challenges facing communities across the country: too many good-paying jobs have disappeared, costs have gone up, and economic opportunity has become harder to find.
That’s why I’m focused on bringing manufacturing back home, strengthening American supply chains, and investing in a 21st-century Heartland economy. By supporting American industry, modernizing our infrastructure, and creating good-paying jobs, we can ensure our communities, and those across the nation, have the opportunity to thrive.
- I was proud to help establish the White House Made in America Office to ensure that American companies and manufacturers get top priority in federal projects.
- In Congress, I launched a Climate Jobs Task Force to focus on building our clean energy economy with good-paying union jobs in places like Central and Southern Illinois.
- Since World War I, a shoe manufacturing company in Belleville has been equipping our military service members with combat boots. During my first term in Congress, I was thrilled to announce nearly $20 million in contracts for Belleville Boots and work on a bipartisan basis to support American military equipment manufacturing in the National Defense Authorization Act.
- I was proud to take on U.S. Steel and demand better for the community of Granite City. Together, with the United Steelworkers, we secured the commitments for long-term security of the mill and watched them rehire 400 workers.
- Our region is also a national leader in the development of cutting-edge agricultural technology. I was proud to advocate for the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign’s Fermentation and Agriculture Bio-manufacturing (IFAB) Hub to receive designation as a national Tech Hub. This designation further establishes the Decatur to Champaign region as America’s Ag Tech Corridor and will help to attract additional federal investment to our region.

pages.title: Supporting Family Farmers - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Supporting Family Farmers
Agriculture is the number one economic driver in Illinois — and communities in Central and Southern Illinois are some of the top producers of corn, soybeans and horseradish in the world. As a member of the House Committee on Agriculture, I’m laser focused on delivering results for our family farmers and rural communities.
I’ve formed a bipartisan Agriculture Advisory Council with stakeholders across the 13th District to help me advocate for a strong, bipartisan farm bill that brings agriculture into the 21st century, supports our family farmers and feeds hungry folks across Illinois. I’ll keep pushing my colleagues to get it done.
- This year, farmers across the country have been squeezed from every direction. Input costs remain stubbornly high, critical export markets are becoming less reliable, and farm bankruptcies are on the rise. Congress must provide the stability and support our agricultural communities need. That’s why I fought for a Farm Bill that would deliver real relief and long-term certainty for farmers.
- I worked to include amendments that protect the Environmental Quality Incentives Program (EQIP), which helps farmers invest in conservation practices that strengthen their operations and protect natural resources. I also fought to preserve farmers’ access to USDA funding for voluntary solar energy projects and to restore critical SNAP funding, which supports families while strengthening demand for the food our farmers produce. While House Republicans refused to include these amendments, our work is far from over. I will continue to push for a better Farm Bill that works for our growers — not one that leaves them behind.
Rebuilding Rural Communities
- From aging infrastructure and a rapidly changing economy to limited access to health care and high-speed internet, our nation’s rural communities are facing an onslaught of generational challenges. In Congress, I’m fighting for investment and support to help our smallest cities and towns survive and thrive in our modern economy. I introduced the Rebuild Rural America Act to invest in economic development and allow the federal government to provide more comprehensive support to rural communities.
- Since coming to Congress, I’ve been proud to fight for local farmers and advance biofuels policy. Higher blends of biofuels help folks save money at the gas pump, reduce our dependence on foreign oil, and cut carbon emissions. It’s also supports critical markets for Illinois family farmers – so many of whom I represent in Congress. That’s why I was proud to introduce the bipartisan Nationwide Consumer and Fuel Retailer Choice Act and see it pass the House with overwhelming support. This is a win for the American people — to deliver lower fuel prices and more certainty for our farmers.
Driving Agriculture Research & Development
- Central and Southern Illinois are home to some of our nation’s leading agricultural research institutions, but our nation’s investment in this research has fallen behind China and the European Union. I’m working to ensure that the United States can continue to lead the world in food production and food security. That’s why I introduced the America Grows Act to put our money where our mouth is and up our investments in the incredible work being done at places like the University of Illinois, Southern Illinois University Edwardsville and the community colleges and agribusinesses throughout our region.
Supporting the Next Generation of Family Farmers
- The average age of an American family farmer is approaching 60 years old, and the success of our rural communities will depend on our next generation entering agriculture. I’ve introduced two bipartisan bills to help bring more young people into the agriculture workforce by making farm and ranch workers eligible for public service student loan forgiveness and help young and beginning farmers gain access to land, markets and capital — the biggest barriers for new and underserved farmers.
Combating Food Deserts
- When residents of Cahokia Heights lost access to their local grocery store, I knew we had to do more to ensure that every family has access to healthy, affordable food options — no matter where they live. I’m proud to be a cosponsor of the Food Deserts Act to support grocery stores in areas with limited food access. I’ve also signed on to support the Delivering for Rural Seniors Act and the Enhance Access to SNAP for College Students Act to address food insecurity for Americans of all ages.

pages.title: Advocating for Veterans - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Advocating for Veterans
As the granddaughter of two World War II veterans and a member of the House Committee on Veterans’ Affairs (HVAC), I’m committed to ensuring that our nation’s heroes receive the benefits they’ve earned and deserve. With the input of my Veterans Advisory Council, I’m working to improve access to services for veterans in our rural communities and to ensure that we’re doing right by our women veterans — the largest growing demographic in the VA system.
In the 119th Congress, I also serve on the HVAC Subcommittee on Technology Modernization, which has oversight and investigative jurisdiction over the Department of Veterans Affairs’ major IT projects and technology modernization programs.
- Veterans deserve a VA that listens to their experiences and responds to their needs. That’s why I was proud to see my bill, the Veterans Office Experience Act, signed into law. The bill ensures veterans, caregivers, and families continue to have a voice in improving VA services, helping make the system more accessible, transparent, and responsive. By strengthening feedback and accountability, this law will help build trust and deliver a better experience for those who have served our country.
- Too often, veterans struggle to access the benefits they’ve earned due to confusing processes and complicated paperwork. This Congress, I introduced the Clear Communication for Veterans Claims Act to streamline the VA’s communication with our veterans and eliminate unnecessary legal jargon. I was pleased to see this bill pass the House and move closer to helping our veterans access the services they deserve.
- When our service members return home, it’s critical that we help them find good-paying careers. I’ve introduced bipartisan legislation to expand veterans’ access to jobs in science, technology and health care by making it easier to access STEM scholarships. I’m glad that this bill has passed unanimously out of the House Veterans Affairs Committee and I’m hopeful that it will soon help us to fill high-demand jobs while ensuring that our heroes have pathways to new careers.
- Many service members suffer invisible wounds upon returning home and the reporting process shouldn’t deepen that pain. I introduced a bipartisan bill, that passed out of the House, that provides much-needed updates to VA training and ensures survivors receive the certainty, compassion, and care they deserve.
- Women veterans are the fastest growing demographic in our veteran community, but they continue to lack quality access to critical health care services. In October 2024, I formed a Women Veterans Advisory Council with women from Central and Southern Illinois to hear directly about the challenges women vets continue to face. I was glad to take their input back to Washington where I held a Congressional women veterans roundtable to discuss how we can better serve our women vets.

pages.title: Protecting Medicare & Social Security - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Protecting Medicare & Social Security
Social Security and Medicare are a promise that we’ve made to America’s workers. As Republicans seek to make cuts to these programs to pay for massive corporate tax breaks, I will continue to oppose any changes that will undercut these vital programs and ensure these programs remain solvent for generations to come.
- During my first term in Congress, I championed the Social Security Fairness Act – bipartisan legislation to close a loophole that prevented those who paid into Social Security from getting the benefits they earned. In December 2024, I joined my colleagues from both sides of the aisle at the White House to watch this bill become law. Now, folks who were impacted by this loophole will start receiving their full benefits.
- Too many of our federal workers – especially postal workers – began in “non-career” positions that never counted toward their retirement. A technical loophole that has kept workers – who’ve kept our country running – from their retirement. I helped reintroduce the Federal Retirement Fairness Act to allow catch-up contributions from time spent in temporary roles, allowing workers to retire on time – with the benefits they’ve earned.
- I’ve also cosponsored the Seniors Access to Critical Medications Act to ensure that patients on Medicare can continue to receive critical medications by mail, and allow caregivers and family members to obtain medications on their behalf.
- Health care, prescription drugs, housing – all continue to rise and these costs hit retirees the hardest. Right now, the current COLA is 2.8 percent – and it’s not enough. That’s why I will continue fighting to pass the Boosting Benefits and COLAs for Seniors Act .
- I’m proud to support giving Medicare the ability to negotiate drug prices, which prevents Big Pharma from ripping off America’s seniors and making taxpayers foot the bill.

pages.title: Investing in Public Safety - Nikki for Congress
pages.text:
## Investing in Public Safety
Investing in public safety is critical in our work to support growth and prosperity in communities across Central and Southern Illinois. That means providing state-of-the-art training for members of law enforcement, recruiting and retaining dedicated first responders, supporting community policing and addressing our nation’s mental health crisis with the urgency it deserves.
- I’ve opposed calls to “defund” the police and supported a variety of federal grant programs that provide more resources to our local law enforcement agencies — particularly those in rural communities.
- If we want to improve public safety, it’s imperative that we provide our local law enforcement with the tools they need to do their jobs and keep people safe. In Congress, I secured $200,000 in new federal funding to the Gillespie Police Department. The funding will be used for key investments in street cameras and other technological upgrades that the community has needed for many years to increase safety for rural families.
- I secured $963,000 for the Champaign community , specifically for the Real-Time Crime Center (RTCC) on the University of Illinois Champaign-Urbana campus. The project would allow for expanded and enhanced prevention, monitoring, and response to crimes in-progress in order to protect students and community members.
- I was proud to be endorsed by the Police Benevolent & Protective Association of Illinois in 2022 — the largest downstate police association made up of full-time and retired sworn police officers.
- I stand firmly with our law enforcement officers who risk their lives to keep us safe. That’s why I opposed President Trump’s decision to pardon those who stormed the Capitol on January 6th. These individuals carried out a violent attack against our officers and our democracy. Granting them pardons and allowing them back into our communities undermines the rule of law and poses a serious threat to public safety.
- There is no doubt that Congress must do more to address the fentanyl crisis – this is not only a public health issue, but a safety issue. I’ve worked across the aisle on solutions to the ongoing addiction and overdose crisis by supporting legislation like the STOP Fentanyl Overdoses Act , the Law Enforcement Officers Preventing Overdose Deaths Act and the Modernizing Opioid Treatment Access Act which would help save lives and support folks in their recovery. This Congress, I will continue working across the aisle to find solutions that will save lives.
